newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-PIOLINE HAS NO REGRETS AFTER SAMPRAS POUNDING.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PIOLINE HAS NO REGRETS AFTER SAMPRAS POUNDING.

text.p: Cedric Pioline was flattened by the Sampras steamroller at Wimbledon on Sunday, but he feels no pain, just a burning desire to play more tennis and improve his game.

"I have much more energy than I had at the start of the tournament" the 28-year-old Frenchman said after Pete Sampras beat him 6-4 6-2 6-4. "It's given me even more will to play, to develop, to improve my game."
The dark, brooding Pioline was the first Frenchman to reach the Wimbledon final since Yvon Petra won the title in 1946 wearing long trousers.

He is only the fourth since open tennis started in 1968 to reach any Grand Slam final. Patrick Proisy lost to Andres Gimeno at the 1972 French Open, Yannick Noah won the French Open in 1983 and Henri Leconte lost there to Mats Wilander in 1988.
Pioline has the distinction of reaching two. In the 1993 U.S. Open he got to the final only to meet Pistol Pete who blew him away in straight sets on that occasion too.
He has enjoyed recent success, winning the Prague tournament earlier this year and lifting the Davis Cup with the French team last December and feels he has a lot to be proud of.
"I played a great tournament," he said. "I proved to myself that I can play well again."
Pioline, who has a reputation for a volatile temperament, has been ranked as high as nine in the world, though he had dropped to 44 going into the tournament.
Although, at 28, he is older than many on the circuit, he believes he has a few more years in him yet.
"I started a little bit later than other players and maybe my mind is fresher and what I did here is really a motivation for me," he said.
Pioline described Sampras as a player with a complete game -- serving, volleying, groundstrokes and mental attitude.
"He showed me what I can improve in my game," the Frenchman said. "He's playing very well but he's not God.
"Perhaps if I'd met a different player...but he was my opponent on the day and it's no use having any regrets."
